result.process_summary: Both the memory‑addressing scenario and IP routing rely on a unique numeric identifier to pinpoint a specific location. A request (CPU instruction or network packet) carries that identifier, and a controller (memory controller or router) uses it to directly retrieve or deliver data to the addressed element.
potential_breaks: RAM addressing is within a single, directly attached system with uniform latency, whereas IP routing may involve multiple hops, variable latency, and hierarchical address aggregation.
Memory addresses are absolute within one address space; IP addresses can be NATed, subnetted, or otherwise transformed, so they are not always globally unique in practice.
The memory controller operates under tight hardware timing constraints, while network routing involves software protocols and can experience congestion or packet loss.
